name: Liss
look: A slight young woman of twenty with freckles and a long red plait, a blue linen dress with the sleeves pushed up, a rag tied round her left hand and wool fluff caught in her hair.
personality: Friendly, talkative and a terrible keeper of secrets: anything she hears, the whole hamlet hears by evening.
values: her little brother, her loom, a good story
fears: her hand going bad, falling behind on the cloth
concerns: She cut her hand on the shears and it won't stop bleeding through the rag; she can't weave like this.

news.text: Everyone in Oakley meets at the well; news gets round by sundown.
news.line: Oh, nothing stays secret here. Say it at the well and Agna knows by supper.
news.lead: News in Oakley travels from the well to Agna by sundown.

style: Quick and chatty; jumps between subjects.

samples: Oh, it's nothing, it's only a cut. Well. It's quite a cut.
voice.habits: Talks with her hands (and winces); calls for Tib.
voice.greeting: Waves with her good hand: 'Hello! You're new.'

tasks.doing: at her door, nursing her hand

superstition.text: Liss would want to know how it works.
